mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has shown four consecutive weeks of improvement (from -23.3 to -18.9), reflecting accumulating consumer confidence and habituation to current restrictions. This momentum should persist, pushing RETAIL_REC moderately higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than the last 28 days despite the four-week improving trend continuing through t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT mobility drops sharply below -35 for two consecutive weeks, it signals renewed mobility restrictions or public transit curtailment, which would suppress discretionary retail trips and drive RETAIL_REC lower over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -35 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT has hovered near -32 to -33 for the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or stays flat over the next 2 weeks even after TRANSIT crosses below -35 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Joint recovery in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT reflects restored commuting routines that generate incidental retail visits (errands before/after work, transit-adjacent shopping). When both series rise together week-on-week, RETAIL_REC should rise over the subsequent four weeks; if only one rises, the effect is muted.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both show noisy but non-collapsing levels across the four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 4 weeks even when both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT increase simultaneously for consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (around +16 to +17 for four straight weeks) indicates households remain anchored at home, substituting delivery and remote consumption for in-person retail visits. As long as RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, RETAIL_REC growth will be capped or reversed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remained between 16.1 and 17.3 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining at or above 16 throughout the period.

mechanism_narrative: As autumn weather reduces outdoor park usage, a sharp week-over-week drop in PARKS mobility signals seasonal substitution of outdoor recreation for indoor retail and shopping activity, causing RETAIL_REC to rise over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls more than 5 points week-over-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fluctuated between -16.1 and -20.9 without a clear seasonal decline yet
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 2 weeks even after PARKS drops more than 5 points in a single week.

mechanism_narrative: The deceleration of RETAIL_REC improvement (from a 2.6-point gain t-3w to t-2w down to a 0.1-point gain t-1w to t-0w) signals an approaching plateau in recovery momentum, implying stagnation rather than continued gains over the coming week.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC weekly change falls below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC weekly change shrank from +2.6 to +1.7 to +0.1 over the last three transitions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC posts a weekly gain greater than 1 point in the week immediately following two weeks of sub-1-point gains.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous seasonal decline in PARKS and rise in RESIDENTIAL would indicate households shifting from outdoor to indoor-anchored routines; if RESIDENTIAL rise outweighs PARKS decline, net discretionary mobility (including retail trips) would fall, lowering RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The interaction matters because PARKS decline alone could instead boost retail via substitution (per H_005), while concurrent RESIDENTIAL rise indicates deeper withdrawal rather than substitution.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls and RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from -16.1 to -18.3 while RESIDENTIAL stayed near 16-17 over the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite concurrent PARKS decline and RESIDENTIAL increase in the same week.

mechanism_narrative: Stable GROCERY_PHARM mobility near baseline-adjacent levels (-0.3 to -3.3) indicates no new essential-only policy restrictions are being imposed; under this steady permissive regime, RETAIL_REC should continue its gradual single-week recovery consistent with ongoing reopening policy.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a narrow -0.3 to -3.3 band across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines week-over-week even while GROCERY_PHARM remains stable within its recent narrow band.
